claims.explanation: Tyrphostin-AG-99 is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and the selectively killed lines are enriched for EGFR-mutant or EGFR-dependent lung cancers (HCC4006, NCIH1650, HCC95, KYSE270) and other RTK/RAS-pathway-driven tumors, while many least-affected lines lack EGFR alterations or carry downstream RAS/BRAF mutations that bypass EGFR blockade. The pattern suggests that sensitivity is driven mainly by EGFR mutation/amplification or high EGFR expression and dependence, with PTEN loss and other PI3K-pathway alterations potentially modulating response.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines are among the most killed and EGFR is the annotated target
EGFR-driven lines depend on EGFR signaling for survival
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least affected, bypassing EGFR dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines are largely in the least-affected group
NRAS-mutant lines appear among less affected tumors
PTEN loss may increase dependence on EGFR/PI3K signaling in some killed lines
PIK3CA-mutant lines appear in both groups but may cooperate with RTK inhibition
TP53 mutation is common across both groups and not selective
MET alteration in HGC27 may provide an EGFR-bypass survival signal
ERBB3 mutation in SNUC5 may enhance ErbB-family dependence
MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is among the most killed lines
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and may reduce EGFR dependence
